g.text: LLM Inference Problems — capacity, bandwidth, allocation, quality
Explained on: Beyond → Inference problems · sessions 02 (memory math), 10 (PagedAttention) | see also comparison / roofline / vram_budget_a100 diagrams
0 · The one equation and the three questions
M_KV = 2 · L · B · T · H_kv · d_h · S
100K tokens -> 6.55 GB (MHA, H_kv=32: 256 KiB/token -> 26.2 GB). GQA shrinks ONE term; six others still scale.
B. BANDWIDTH - can HBM feed the cores?
AI = FLOPs/Bytes ; low AI -> memory wall
C. QUALITY - keep accuracy while shrinking?
MQA GQA MLA CLA YOCO SSM FP8-KV
KV + weights must be resident -> OOM if not
KV is re-read every token -> TPOT
KV management sits in the middle
KV cache is simultaneously Capacity + Bandwidth + Latency + Concurrency + Scheduling + Quality.
1 MHA creates a huge KV cache
PROBLEM: H_Q = H_K = H_V = 32: every head keeps its own K/V history. KV grows linearly
with context T and with batch B.
B = 256 KiB/token -> 100K tokens = 26.2 GB at B=1.
FIX: Share K/V across heads: GQA (H_kv 32 -> 8: 64 KiB/token, 6.55 GB) or MQA (H_kv=1:
COST: Only the H_kv term shrinks; K/V diversity drops (quality card 16).
2 Context growth: KV is linear in T
PROBLEM: Even after GQA, M_KV is proportional to T. 4K is fine, 100K is large, 1M is
enormous: long context becomes a CAPACITY problem.
FIX: Cut T (window / eviction), cut bytes per token (MLA, FP8), or stop caching in most
COST: Each fix trades away exact long-range retrieval or quality (cards 14, 19, 21,
PROBLEM: KV cache is a CONCURRENCY problem, not only a context problem: a GPU that
holds one long request cannot hold many.
WHY (math): KV_total = B * KV_1seq. Per seq 6.55 GB: B=1 6.55 | B=4 26.2 | B=8 52.4 GB.
A100-40GB minus 14 GB weights leaves 26 GB; B=4 needs 4 x 6.55 = 26.2 GB -> B<=3 even
before runtime overhead (B_max = 3 with ~4 GB overhead).
FIX: Admission control by real sequence lengths, paged allocation, GQA/MLA, FP8 KV.
COST: Lower concurrency means fewer tokens/s per GPU, so higher $ per token.
4 VRAM capacity: it is not Weights + KV
PROBLEM: 40 GB is physical capacity; the budget also holds activations, CUDA workspace,
WHY (math): 40 GB = Weights + KV + Activations + Workspace + Runtime + Fragmentation.
Example: 14 + 10 + 3 + 2 + 2 = 31 GB, so the 'free' 9 GB is not really free.
FIX: Reserve headroom (e.g. gpu_memory_utilization), size KV pool after profiling peak
COST: Headroom is capacity you cannot use for KV; too little means OOM under bursts.
PROBLEM: Model size, context and concurrency fight for the same HBM. 7B FP16 = 14 GB;
70B FP16 = 140 GB cannot fit one A100-40GB.
FIX: Weight quantization, tensor parallelism / multi-GPU, then shrink KV (GQA/MLA/FP8).
COST: Quantized weights risk quality; multi-GPU adds NVLink/PCIe traffic and cost.
Takeaway: KV cache is a concurrency problem, not merely a context-length problem. Model size <-> context <-> concurrency compete for one
Long context after GQA is still a memory-CAPACITY problem: 64 KiB/token * 1M = 61 GiB.
2 · BANDWIDTH — can HBM feed the cores? (cards 6-11)
PROBLEM: Even when KV fits, every generated token must read the whole historical K/V
from HBM. Decode becomes memory-bandwidth bound.
WHY (math): t_decode >= KV bytes / BW. A100 1.555 TB/s: GQA-8 6.55 GB -> 4.2 ms/token;
MHA 26.2 GB -> 16.8 ms/token; MQA 0.82 GB -> 0.53 ms.
FIX: Move fewer bytes: GQA/MQA, MLA, FP8 KV, sliding window, FlashAttention-style
COST: Same quality/retrieval trade-offs as the capacity fixes (a byte saved is
PROBLEM: nvidia-smi says 35% util and you assume the GPU is wasted. It may simply be
waiting on memory: Tensor Cores idle while KV streams in.
WHY (math): AI_attn ~ H_q/H_kv; P = min(P_compute, AI*BW). A100 (312 TF, 1.555 TB/s):
FIX: Judge by the roofline: compare AI to the ridge, watch HBM-bandwidth utilization,
COST: Util % only says a kernel is running, not how well Tensor Cores are fed.
8 More FLOPS do not fix decode
PROBLEM: GPU B has 2x Tensor FLOPS but only 1.2x memory bandwidth. A memory-bound
WHY (math): Perf ~ AI*BW, not P_compute. 2x compute, 1.2x BW -> ~1.2x decode at best.
AI=10: GPU A (1000 TF, 500 GB/s) = 5 TF; GPU B (500 TF, 1000 GB/s) = 10 TF.
FIX: Pick hardware by bandwidth for decode; first reduce bytes (AI up) rather than buy
COST: High-bandwidth GPUs cost more; FLOPS still matter for prefill and large batches.
9 Prefill vs decode are different problems
PROBLEM: One optimisation does not help both phases: prefill is big GEMMs, decode is
one token plus a huge KV read.
WHY (math): Prefill: AI grows with prompt length T -> compute-bound. Decode GEMV: AI ~
FIX: Prefill: Tensor Cores, FlashAttention, BF16/FP8. Decode: GQA/MQA, KV quant, paged
KV, continuous batching. Optional prefill/decode disaggregation.
COST: Disaggregation needs KV transfer between pools and more scheduling complexity.
PROBLEM: Two production metrics with different bottlenecks: you can have excellent TTFT
with poor TPOT, or the reverse.
WHY (math): TTFT = queueing + tokenization + prefill (compute). TPOT = decode step = KV
bytes moved / BW + weights bytes / BW (memory).
FIX: TTFT: prefill throughput, prefix caching, queue control. TPOT: fewer KV bytes,
continuous batching, speculative decoding (fewer target-model steps).
COST: Bigger decode batches raise throughput but also per-token latency; speculative
11 Fewer bytes = higher AI (the bandwidth fixes)
PROBLEM: Memory-bound decode: raise AI = FLOPs/Bytes without changing the GPU. (Window:
fewer bytes AND FLOPs, AI unchanged.)
WHY (math): FP8 KV: 1 GB -> 0.5 GB for the same 10 GFLOPs: AI 10 -> 20. Window 128K ->
8K: 16x fewer KV bytes AND FLOPs (AI unchanged, TPOT down). GQA-8 of 32: AI x4 on the
FIX: GQA/MQA, FP8 KV, sliding window, data reuse, kernel fusion, FlashAttention.
COST: Precision error (FP8), lost distant tokens (window), quality (GQA/MQA).
Rule: AI < ridge -> attack MEMORY (bytes, reuse, quant).
AI > ridge -> attack COMPUTE (Tensor Cores, precision, FLOPs).
Decode attention stays memory-bound even with MQA (AI 32 << 200).
3 · ALLOCATION — where do the bytes live? (cards 12-15)
PROBLEM: Requests of 37,000 / 4,500 / 19,000 tokens arrive, one finishes, a
12,000-token one arrives. Contiguous max_len allocation leaves holes: enough free VRAM
WHY (math): Pre-allocating max_len per request wastes internal + external
fragmentation: old systems used only 20.4-38.2% of KV memory for real token states
FIX: Allocate KV in fixed blocks (PagedAttention) instead of one contiguous slab.
COST: Extra indirection (block table) in the attention kernel.
PROBLEM: Need dynamic allocation, easy sharing and better batching without moving
WHY (math): Block = 16 tokens; Llama-3-8B block (all layers) = 16 * 128 KiB = 2 MiB.
Waste <= block_size-1 tokens per sequence -> < 4%. 2-4x throughput vs FasterTransformer
FIX: Block table maps logical blocks -> physical blocks; blocks are allocated on demand
COST: Paging does NOT reduce the mathematical amount of KV; it only fixes memory
management. Block size trades waste vs kernel efficiency.
PROBLEM: 1,000,000 tokens cannot all stay in HBM. Which entries remain, get compressed,
WHY (math): Sliding window: M_KV ~ W not T. W=8K vs T=128K -> 16x smaller (toy 64
KiB/tok: 8 GiB -> 512 MiB). Also attention sinks, H2O / token eviction, KV compression,
FIX: Keep sinks + recent window, evict low-attention tokens, offload cold blocks, or
COST: Memory reduction <-> information retention: any evicted token may be the one
PROBLEM: 1,000 users share one 2K-token system prompt; recomputing the same prefix is
WHY (math): No cache: 1000 * 2K = 2M prefill tokens and 1000 * 250 MiB (2000 tok * 128
KiB) = ~244 GiB of KV. Cache: prefill 2K once, store 250 MiB once, share by ref-count.
FIX: Hash token blocks, share physical blocks across requests (enable_prefix_caching).
COST: Needs cache identity (hash), reference counting, eviction policy, memory sharing
4 · QUALITY — can we keep the model's retrieval ability? (cards 16-19)
PROBLEM: Memory efficiency <-> attention representation diversity. GQA/MQA keep Q heads
WHY (math): MHA: 32 distinct K/V per layer. GQA-8: K_1 = K_2 = K_3 = K_4 within a group
(Q_i != Q_j). MQA: all 32 Q heads see ONE K/V.
FIX: Pick an intermediate H_kv (GQA); MLA keeps more structure at a small cache.
COST: Fewer distinct K/V representations; quality can degrade.
PROBLEM: H_kv = 1: 32x smaller KV, but every head reads the same K/V representation.
WHY (math): A_i = softmax(Q_i K^T / sqrt(d_h)) still differs per head via Q_i (K:
B,T,1,d_h shared), but the K/V content is identical. GQA paper: MQA can degrade
FIX: GQA as the middle point (e.g. 4 Q heads per KV head).
COST: Quality loss, harder to train stably; use only when memory dominates.
PROBLEM: There is no universal optimal ratio; it is an architecture-search problem
balancing quality, KV memory, bandwidth, latency.
FIX: Retrofit: uptrain MHA -> GQA by mean-pooling K_g = mean(K_i in group), ~5% of
COST: Ratio is baked into weights; changing it later means more uptraining.
PROBLEM: Store KV in FP8 (1 B) or lower instead of FP16 (2 B): half the bytes to hold
WHY (math): S: 2 -> 1 -> KV_FP8 ~ KV_FP16 / 2 (toy GQA-8: 6.55 -> 3.28 GB) and AI x2
FIX: Per-head / per-channel scales, outlier handling, quality-sensitive layers kept in
COST: Attention-score error, long-context degradation, numerical instability,
5 · ARCHITECTURE FIXES — change what is cached (cards 20-23)
PROBLEM: GQA 32 -> 8 gives r = 32/8 = 4 and M_KV down 4x. But L, B, T, d_h and S are
WHY (math): M_KV = 2*L*B*T*H_kv*d_h*S: GQA changes H_kv only. KV still ~ T and ~ L.
FIX: Attack the other terms: S (FP8), T (window), L (CLA/YOCO), H_kv*d_h (MLA), token
COST: Each term needs its own method, its own retraining level and its own quality
21 MLA: cache a latent, not K/V
PROBLEM: GQA shares heads; the representation H_kv*d_h is still stored. Can we compress
WHY (math): Cache c^KV = W^DKV h (512) + k^R (64) = 576 elem/token/layer vs MHA
FIX: Low-rank latent + decoupled RoPE key; absorb W^UK / W^UV into Q and W^O at decode.
COST: From scratch or MHA->MLA conversion (joint SVD, partial RoPE; Llama-2-7B -92.19%
KV, ~0.5% LongBench drop). Needs MLA-specific kernels.
PROBLEM: Standard Transformer keeps independent KV in all L layers (the factor L). Do
adjacent layers really need distinct KV?
WHY (math): CLA: layer pairs share one KV -> L_eff = L/2 (paper: ~2x smaller than MQA,
near-equal accuracy). YOCO: self-decoder builds ONE global KV reused by cross-decoder
FIX: Share KV across layers (CLA) or cache once (YOCO).
COST: Changes the learned computation graph: Level-3 retraining; layers lose private
PROBLEM: Do most layers need token-level KV at all? Replace it with a recurrent state
s_t = f(s_{t-1}, x_t), fixed size in T.
WHY (math): Qwen3-Next 3:1 DeltaNet:Gated-Attn -> only 25% of layers keep KV (48 layers
FIX: Keep exact retrieval in a few attention layers, cheap state elsewhere ('attention
COST: Compressed state can forget exact facts ('5th number in paragraph 72'); Level-3
6 · The complete problem statement and objective
subject to Weights + KV + Activation + Workspace < VRAM
and, in memory-bound regimes: Latency_decode ~ KV bytes moved / Memory Bandwidth
Maximise useful tokens/sec/$ with finite capacity, finite bandwidth, finite compute, and dynamically changing KV needs.
PagedAttention, FlashAttention, KV quantization, continuous batching, prefix caching.
MHA -> GQA (~5% compute), MHA -> MQA, MHA -> MLA (SVD + partial RoPE).
Transformer -> hybrid attention/SSM, full-KV layers -> cross-layer sharing.

Single most important insight: KV cache is not merely a storage problem. It is Capacity + Bandwidth + Latency + Concurrency + Scheduling + Quality at once - modern LLM architecture is about controlling information movement through the GPU memory hierarchy, not merely adding FLOPS.
